claims.text: Introducing a nanohierarchical cooperative heterostructure into CoCrFeNi will enable low wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
Introducing the cooperative heterostructure into CoCrFeNi will maintain a low coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can create the proposed nanohierarchical structure in CoCrFeNi.
The proposed structure contains A1-to-A3 nano-coupled grains interspersed with A2 nanoprecipitates.
The proposed nano-coupled grains are equiaxed and the nanoprecipitates are uniformly distributed.
A load of approximately 10 N is typical for the stated ball-on-disk or pin-on-disc testing configuration.
The cooperative heterostructure creates graded frictional-stress distributions during wear.
At room temperature, nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates permit multiple deformation pathways that release frictional stress in stages.
The room-temperature staged stress-release mechanism reduces wear.
The room-temperature staged stress-release mechanism reduces the coefficient of friction.
At elevated temperature, the nanohierarchical structure promotes tribo-reaction and formation of a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer.
The protective nanocrystalline glaze layer forms rapidly across the elevated-temperature portion of the test regime.
The high-temperature nanocrystalline glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear.
Relative to conventional CoCrFeNi, the engineered CoCrFeNi will have lower wear rates throughout the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
Relative to conventional CoCrFeNi, the engineered CoCrFeNi will have lower coefficients of friction throughout the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The engineered structure will improve load-bearing capability.
Conventional CoCrFeNi typically develops increased friction and severe high-temperature wear because of surface softening and oxidation.
The nanohierarchical cooperative-heterostructure strategy may be transferable from the demonstrated Ni-based complex concentrated alloy to other alloy systems.
